conversation.text:
## Good news! You are **ELIGIBLE** for Child Benefit for both children.

### For Alex (4 years old):
Even though Alex doesn't live with you, you qualify for Child Benefit because you are contributing £50.00 per week towards Alex's upkeep. This exceeds the Child Benefit payment amount, and according to government guidance, you can continue receiving Child Benefit when you contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment. Since no other claimant has priority and Alex meets all other requirements (not in care, not in hospital, etc.), you are eligible.

### For Blake (14 years old):
Blake lives with you and is under 16, which makes eligibility straightforward. Blake meets all the requirements and has no disqualifying circumstances.

### Important notes:
- Only one person can claim Child Benefit for each child, so make sure no one else is claiming for either Alex or Blake
- You'll need to inform HMRC if your contributions towards Alex's upkeep stop or fall below the Child Benefit amount
- If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge

You can proceed with your Child Benefit application for both children!

reasonings: Alex is 4 years old (under 16), which meets the age requirement. Although Alex does not live with you, you are contributing £50.00 per week towards Alex's upkeep. According to the guidance on 'Child Benefit if your child lives with someone else', you can continue to receive Child Benefit beyond the initial 8 weeks if you contribute to your child's upkeep by the same amount or more than the Child Benefit payment. Current Child Benefit rates are approximately £25.60 per week for the eldest child and £16.95 for additional children, so your contribution of £50.00/week exceeds the Child Benefit amount. The guidance confirms that 'upkeep includes clothes, presents, food and pocket money and financial contributions to provide your child with somewhere to live.' Additionally, no other claimant has priority, the child is not in local authority care, hospital, or residential accommodation, is not fostered, does not work 24+ hours/week, has not started an apprenticeship, and does not receive qualifying benefits. You live in the UK, which satisfies the residency requirement. Therefore, you meet all the eligibility criteria for Alex.

Blake is 14 years old (under 16) and lives with you, which satisfies the basic eligibility requirements. According to the main eligibility guidance, 'You normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK. You'll usually be responsible for a child if you live with them.' Blake is not in local authority care, hospital, or residential accommodation, is not fostered, does not work 24+ hours/week, has not started an apprenticeship, and does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right. You live in the UK, which satisfies the residency requirement. Therefore, you meet all the eligibility criteria for Blake.
